newInPhase22.area: One-Click Care handlers — Windows IPC round trip
newInPhase22.debt: The four care request handlers and the CareCoordinator were exercised through unit + integration tests on the development host. The desktop ↔ named-pipe ↔ LocalSystem-service round trip with a real authenticated principal has not run for these handlers.
newInPhase22.closurePath: Ride the existing Windows qualification lane; assert principal scoping, consent gating, single-flight rejection under concurrent start, and journal completeness.

newInPhase22.area: Live domain dispatch inside the orchestrator run path
newInPhase22.debt: Phase 22 ships the complete orchestration machinery (composition, firewall, single-flight lease, journaled resume, fence cancellation, truth-first report) exercised against the DomainStepExecutor trait boundary. Binding each domain coordinator's headless start_with_lease entry point into the orchestrator's execution thread is intentionally deferred: several coordinators currently assume the router's async watch context.
newInPhase22.closurePath: Expose headless entry points per domain (or a dispatcher service-side), then flip ServiceExecutor to call them. Until then live runs surface an explicit typed rejection instead of a fabricated success.
newInPhase22.honestyNote: This is the load-bearing debt of Phase 22: the UI can compose plans, grant session consent, cancel, and read evidence-based reports, but a live end-to-end mutation sequence requires this wiring.

newInPhase22.area: Session consent scope semantics on Windows service restart
newInPhase22.debt: Consent lives in an in-memory registry keyed by principal. A service restart mid-session clears it (conservative and safe), but the UX copy does not yet distinguish 'consent cleared by service restart' from 'never granted'.
newInPhase22.closurePath: Add a distinct status reason key once native round-trip testing lands.
